votes.motion: Accept the gift of $895 from the Kevin T. Zozek Memorial Scholarship for Financial Trust to Lunenburg athletics/middle school athletic department
Accept the business administrator employment contract for Chris McNamera

budget_items.what_was_said: A gift from the Kevin T. Zozek Memorial Scholarship for Financial Trust was presented to Lunenburg athletics, intended for the middle school athletic department; Zozek was a student athlete who died on 9/11.
The committee moved to formally approve the employment contract for newly hired business administrator Chris McNamera, following discussion in executive session.

The presenter described the committee's fiscal policy role over the year, including optional quarterly budget reporting, approving transfers between cost centers, and signing warrants, as part of a broader financial check-and-balance system.

A member asked whether consolidating facilities with the town would mean losing budget authority while the school budget still pays maintenance salaries; the presenter said such mergers rarely save money unless a whole administrator position is eliminated.

decisions.decision: The committee announced it had already decided to hire Chris McNamera as the district's business administrator.
The committee tentatively agreed to target June for the superintendent's evaluation cycle this year.
The committee agreed to hold a follow-up discussion at a future meeting to plan the calendar and process for the superintendent's evaluation.

minutes.headline: Committee approved business administrator's contract; then trained with MASC on evaluating the new superintendent.
minutes.summary: This was a workshop meeting: the committee welcomed and approved a contract for newly hired business administrator Chris McNamera, accepted a $895 memorial-scholarship gift to athletics, then spent most of the meeting in a MASC-led training on the division between school committee and superintendent roles and on how to structure the new superintendent's annual evaluation under state regulation. No budget votes or major policy decisions were made beyond the personnel and donation items; the committee agreed to hold a follow-up discussion to set a calendar for the superintendent evaluation process.

what_happened.line: Committee approved the employment contract for newly hired business administrator Chris McNamera, though the vote outcome was not clearly audible on the recording.
Committee accepted a memorial scholarship gift directed to middle school athletics.
Most of the meeting was a MASC-led training on the line between school committee and superintendent roles, not a policy vote.
The training covered how to structure the new superintendent's annual evaluation under state regulation, with a tentative target of June for the cycle.
Committee agreed to hold a follow-up meeting to set the calendar and process for that evaluation.

why_it_matters: The business administrator oversees day-to-day district finances, so the terms of this contract shape how school budget matters are managed going forward.
How the superintendent is evaluated -- and on what timeline -- affects district leadership accountability that residents may see surface at future public meetings.
The athletics gift adds outside funding to middle school sports rather than drawing on the town budget.
